coordinates.locator: src:bnl-rhic-complex-page states the ring has six interaction points and that detectors remain at two of them; coordinate value is the ROR campus geocode (src:bnl-ror-record, listed in this record's top-level `sources`, not `coordinates.sources`, since a geocoder source may only back a campus/headquarters coordinate kind per A17) used as a fallback anchor.
coordinates.note: Per amendment A23, this site is honestly recorded as a campus-grade point (kind: campus, confidence: approximate) because no rank<=7 source with an explicit geodetic coordinate for the STAR interaction-region hall specifically was found and fetched in this session: two technical PDFs (agsrhichome.bnl.gov/RHIC/RAP/rhic_notes/AD-RHIC-1-142/RHIC_OVERVIEW.pdf and .../RHIC/Spin/design/chap4.pdf) and a DOE NEPA document (energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-04/fonsi-ea-2138-electron-ion-collider-bnl-2021-03-25.pdf) returned only unreadable/corrupted binary content; the official experiment sites star.bnl.gov and phenix.bnl.gov returned HTTP 403; and the official bnl.gov RHIC pages describe the ring's six interaction points and confirm detectors remain at two of them in prose only, without coordinates or a clock position. The lat/lon recorded is the BNL campus centroid (ROR geocode, src:bnl-ror-record, cited in this record's top-level `sources` only, not in `coordinates.sources`, since a geocoder may back only campus/headquarters kinds per A17); `precision_m` is widened to bound the RHIC ring's own ~0.6 km radius (from the sourced 2.4 mi / 3.86 km circumference). The PHENIX detector's Wikipedia infobox gives 40.8831 N, 72.8817 W (src:bnl-rhic-phenix-wikipedia, rank 12, corroboration only, not a coordinate source), about 1.6 km from this point, consistent with a campus-grade estimate. A future agent with a surveyed or technical-document coordinate for this interaction point should replace this value.

name: RHIC Interaction Point 6 (STAR experimental hall)
notes: STAR has operated continuously at this interaction point since RHIC's first collisions in 2000 through RHIC's final run on 2026-02-06 (src:heavy-ions-rhic-final-collisions-2026).

Multiple secondary sources (search-engine summaries of physics papers, not independently re-fetched and verified in this session) describe this as RHIC's 6 o'clock interaction point; that specific clock-position label is not recorded as a sourced fact here because no rank<=7 source stating it was successfully fetched.

summary.plain: The experimental hall on the RHIC particle-collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory where the STAR detector records the debris of particle collisions.
summary.technical: One of the two interaction-region halls that remained active on the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider ring at Brookhaven National Laboratory, housing the STAR detector from RHIC's first collisions (2000) through its final run (2026). A geodetic fix for this interaction point specifically was not found in this session; the coordinate recorded is the laboratory's campus-level point (see note).
